title: OpenAI quietly signs letter from Nvidia, Microsoft, and Meta warning about dangers of 'premature restrictions' on open-weight AI models — as the White House accuses China of stealing from Anthropic
excerpt: With China's open-weight AI models continuing to improve, US companies want to see a free market for all.
content_html:
• Several AI companies in the US have published an open letter
  • The letter is campaigning for unrestricted open-weight AI
  • Meanwhile the US government accuses Moonshot AI of IP theft

Any hopes AI tech reporters may have had about easing quietly into the weekend have been dashed by some of the biggest names in the business sharing an open letter in support of open-weight AI models — while the White House has accused China of 'large scale' theft from US companies in building its open-weight AI.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got the ball rolling with his first-ever tweet, linking to a statement championing open-weight AI models, those models that can be downloaded, viewed, and edited by anyone. Models like this are essential for making AI "more accessible, adaptable, and widely available" the open letter says.

It's co-signed by a slew of well-known tech and AI companies, including Meta, Microsoft, Perplexity, and IBM. While ChatGPT developer OpenAI — which has had more of a closed-model focus, to date — didn't appear on the original post from Huang, it has now also backed the sentiments.

Essentially, these companies are campaigning for openness in AI to drive innovation and access, while also arguing against 'premature restrictions' by governments. It's no coincidence that the US government led by President Trump has recently tried to take a more prominent role in evaluating AI models and deciding when they should be released.

It's also notable that Anthropic and Google are missing from the list of backers to this open letter. We don't have any official comment yet from these companies, so it's hard to judge the reasoning — Google regularly releases open AI models, after all — but it could be something to do with recent accusations aimed at Moonshot AI in China.

Open and closed

Part of the background to this open letter is that Chinese company Moonshot AI stands accused of distilling Claude's (closed) Fable 5 model in order to build its own (open) Kimi K3. In simple terms, distilling works by asking millions of questions of an AI model, and using the responses as training data.

It's something Moonshot AI has denied, while hyping up the potential of the open-weighted, freely downloadable Kimi K3 AI model, which is being released on Monday — another factor in this open letter coming out now. The US government is calling it IP theft, and has issued some heavy-handed responses.

"We support open-source AI and the innovation it unlocks," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent posted on X. "But open source is not open season on American IP. When PRC firms conduct covert, industrial-scale distillation attacks that cross the line into IP theft, sanctions and Entity List designations will be on the table."

What Nvidia, Meta, Microsoft, and the other open letter co-signers seem to be doing is trying to get ahead of any potential clampdown by the US government on open-weighted models. While everyone agrees that these AI models are beneficial, it's not clear what the next regulatory steps might be.

However, the open letter is vague and general enough that you can read between the lines in a variety of different ways. It may be intended to allude to the Moonshot AI case, or it may not. What's clear is that we're coming to a crunch point for AI regulation and innovation across the globe, and everyone has a perspective.

content_html_zh:
• 美国多家AI公司发表公开信
  • 这封信是为了争取不受限制的开放式人工智能
  • 与此同时，美国政府指控 Moonshot AI 盗窃知识产权

人工智能科技记者对周末悄然放松的希望已经被业内一些大人物分享了一封支持开放权重人工智能模型的公开信所破灭——而白宫则指责中国在构建开放权重人工智能时“大规模”盗窃美国公司的资金。

Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 发布了他的第一条推文，链接到一份支持开放权重人工智能模型的声明，这些模型可以被任何人下载、查看和编辑。 公开信称，这样的模型对于让人工智能“更容易获得、适应性更强、更广泛可用”至关重要。

它由许多知名科技和人工智能公司联合签署，包括 Meta、微软、Perplexity 和 IBM。 虽然 ChatGPT 开发商 OpenAI（迄今为止，它更多地关注封闭模型）并未出现在 Huang 的原始帖子中，但它现在也支持了这种观点。

从本质上讲，这些公司正在推动人工智能的开放，以推动创新和准入，同时也反对政府的“过早限制”。 特朗普总统领导的美国政府最近试图在评估人工智能模型并决定何时发布它们方面发挥更重要的作用，这并非巧合。

还值得注意的是，这封公开信的支持者名单中缺少 Anthropic 和 Google。 我们还没有这些公司的任何官方评论，所以很难判断其中的原因——毕竟谷歌定期发布开放的人工智能模型——但这可能与最近针对中国 Moonshot AI 的指控有关。

打开和关闭

这封公开信的部分背景是，中国公司 Moonshot AI 被指控提炼克劳德的（封闭的）《神鬼寓言 5》模型，以构建自己的（开放的）Kimi K3。 简单来说，提炼的工作原理是向人工智能模型提出数百万个问题，并将答案用作训练数据。

Moonshot AI 否认了这一点，同时大肆宣传周一发布的开放权重、可免费下载的 Kimi K3 AI 模型的潜力——这是现在发表的公开信中的另一个因素。 美国政府称其为知识产权盗窃，并做出了一些严厉的回应。

订阅突发新闻、评论、观点、顶级技术交易等。

美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 在 X 上发帖称：“我们支持开源人工智能及其带来的创新。” “但开源并不是美国知识产权的开放季节。 当中国公司进行秘密的、工业规模的精炼攻击并跨越知识产权盗窃的界限时，制裁和实体名单指定将摆在桌面上。”

英伟达、Meta、微软和其他公开信共同签署者似乎正在做的事情是试图抢先于美国政府对开放加权模型的任何潜在限制。 虽然每个人都同意这些人工智能模型是有益的，但目前尚不清楚下一步的监管措施可能是什么。

然而，这封公开信的内容非常模糊和笼统，你可以通过多种不同的方式阅读字里行间的内容。 它可能是为了暗示 Moonshot AI 案例，也可能不是。 显而易见的是，我们正处于全球人工智能监管和创新的关键时刻，每个人都有自己的观点。
